correctness.rationale: PASS: Multiplying the Cesàro matrix C gives (C²)_{nk}=(H_n-H_{k-1})/n for k≤n, whereas W2_{nk}=log(n/k)/n; telescoping yields D_{nk}=1/n²+(1/n) sum_{ell=k}^{n-1} a_ell with a_ell=1/ell-log(1+1/ell)∈(0,1/(2ell²)]. The operator identity D=Q+sum_{ell≥1} a_ell u_ell⊗v_ell*, Q=diag(n^-2), u_ell=sum_{n>ell}e_n/n, v_ell=sum_{k≤ell}e_k, is trace-norm convergent because norm(u_ell)norm(v_ell)≤1 and sum a_ell<∞. For 1/2<p≤1, the p-quasi triangle inequality yields ||D||_Sp^p≤(1+2^-p)ζ(2p); for p>1 trace class implies membership. Conversely finite N compressions are triangular with eigenvalues exactly n^-2, so eigenvalue–singular-value log-majorization valid for ALL p>0 forces sum_{n≤N}n^-2p≤||D||_Sp^p whenever D∈Sp; divergence for p≤1/2 proves necessity and the stated lower bound. Trace-class compression convergence gives Fredholm determinant Π(1-z/n²)=sin(pi sqrt(z))/(pi sqrt(z)), hence simple nonzero eigenvalues. Independent finite matrix identities/triangular eigenvalues, SVD lower inequalities for N=8,16,32,64 and p=.4,.55,.75,1 checked. This does not claim pointwise singular-value asymptotics.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified: Bellavita–Stylogiannis 2026 introduced the sampled Mellin algebra and gave generic Hilbert–Schmidt multiplicativity defects while discussing Schatten refinements. The 2026-09-19 Resultary theorem fully read establishes trace class and ζ(2) trace for the exact operator D and all integer convolution semigroup defects; consequently the present claim is not new for p≥1 or its trace, which it explicitly credits. The exact quasi-Schatten threshold p=1/2, sharp two-sided quasi norm bounds, and determinant simplification were not found in the inspected earlier primary work. The related Cesàro self-commutator p>1/3 concerns C*C-CC*, not C²-W2. Residual exact triangular-operator quasi-ideal literature could give an equivalent cutoff.

value.rationale: PASS: The critical quasi-Schatten exponent is a natural singular-value regularity invariant of a canonical lattice-versus-Mellin product defect, and extends earlier trace-class classification into a genuinely finer, nonlocally convex ideal scale. The 1/2 cutoff is sharp for the complete positive-exponent range and has a substantive finite-compression obstruction; it is not just a restatement of the known trace. No unsupported individual singular-value asymptotic is asserted.
